subject: Command handoff: weekly wins, blockers, QBR prep
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Command handoff: weekly wins, blockers, QBR prep

Team — quick handoff before EOD. Keeping this tight so leadership can use it in the QBR pack. TL;DR at top, details below.

TL;DR
- Wins: Hosted API latency improvement (p50 down 18%), closed two Dedicated pilot commitments (Acme & NovaPay).
- Risks: One prioritization risk on Dedicated autoscaler (capacity shortfall if trial ramps), a pending procurement SLA exception for Acme.
- Asks: 1) Ops: validate staging autoscaler config (Jonas). 2) Sales/Legal: finalize SLA exception packet & DocuSign routing (Karthik). 3) Leadership: sign off on conservative guidance for QBR (Laura).

DETAILED UPDATES
1) Product / Infra (Jonas)
- What went well: We shipped the attention-kernel micro-ops that reduced p50 token latency from 98ms to 80ms on the hosted L7 routes. Customer-facing perf tests look good — sample traces attached.
- Open: Autoscaler policy for Dedicated pools currently assumes steady arrival rate; we saw a 3x burst pattern in Acme pilot load tests yesterday that caused 30s warmup tail. If we can't shorten warmup, we should set a temporary burst reserve.
- Impact: Without mitigation, forecasted 48-hour peak could breach the QBR latency SLO for Dedicated trials.

2) Sales / GTM (Karthik)
- Closed deals: Acme (pilot commit, reserve 4 cards) and NovaPay (pilot verbal). Both are signature-in-progress — procurement asked for an SLA exception covering key rotation & retention window.
- Ask: Need an SLA exception packet and DocuSign routing by COB Monday. I can push the commercial terms but need legal signoff on exception language.

3) Leadership / Ops (Neha)
- QBR prep items: Please review the attached QBR_checklist_v2.xlsx — I updated the "Risk Mitigations" tab with proposed wording for leadership.
- Escalation lane: If we can't reduce autoscaler warmup by Friday, we'll propose a temporary reserve and note expected cost impact in the QBR appendix.

Attachments referenced: QBR_checklist_v2.xlsx (sheet: Risks + data), SLA_exception_request.pdf (procurement packet stub)

Next steps (asks + owners):
- Jonas: run a quick experiment to reduce GPU warmup (kernel pre-load) and share numbers by Tue noon.
- Karthik: assemble SLA exception packet and request legal review; loop in procurement and get DocuSign link.
- Laura: quick sign-off on messaging for leadership (conservative forecast vs optimistic) — aim to lock by Tue EOD.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0173

-----Original Message-----
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, mina.haddad@redwood.ai <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 16:10:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Command handoff: weekly wins, blockers, QBR prep

Neha — thanks for the roundup. Quick datapoints from infra: 
- The 3x burst came from Acme's batch ingest test; we can reduce tail by 12–15% if we enable kernel pre-warm and extend the KV cache to cold-start differently, but that will add ~6% memory pressure on the Dedicated nodes.
- Experiment plan: I can run A/B on the staging pool (pre-warm on vs off) and share traces by Monday morning.

Also flagging a secondary risk: if NovaPay ramps earlier than expected (they said they could be north of the pilot numbers), we may need to throttle by tier which will require a small API change. If that happens, it'll affect the "seamless" demo narrative in the QBR.

Jonas
Director, Serving Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 17:08:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Command handoff: weekly wins, blockers, QBR prep

Adding procurement context — from Acme: procurement@acme.com asked for explicit retention windows and a key-rotation cadence in the SLA exception. I drafted a short packet (attached) but legal needs to review specific language around on-prem key custody.

Action items for me:
- I'll circulate the SLA_exception_request.pdf to Legal and Procurement now.
- I'll create the DocuSign envelope once legal signs off (should be able to do this by Mon EOD if there are no major redlines).

One more ask for the QBR: can Infra supply a simple slide with two scenarios (conservative vs optimistic) for latency/cost impact if we apply the temporary reserve? I can place that in the appendix.

—Karthik
VP, Sales — Midmarket & Strategic Accounts
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 18:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Command handoff: weekly wins, blockers, QBR prep

Thanks — this is clear and actionable. Laura here — I approve the conservative framing for the QBR. We should be transparent about the potential cost delta for the temporary reserve and call out the remediation plan (Jonas's experiment + throttle plan).

Mina — please take point on the leadership slide text; keep it to one paragraph with a single appendix slide containing numbers.

I'll fold this into the QBR pack after you share the appendix.

Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

"The best defense is a clear ask."
